A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same survey, with readable text, figures, tables, and complete end matter. All 85 pages of v8 and 91 pages of v10 support comparison. Neither PDF contains a separately labeled appendix.

before.justification: v8 provides literature synthesis and descriptive catalogues, without original experimental or quantitative data-analysis results. Performance findings are attributed to cited work; Figure 24's example scores are explicitly illustrative.

after.justification: v10 remains a descriptive survey. Its additional performance findings concern cited systems, without experiments or empirical analyses conducted by the survey authors. Figure 27 retains the illustrative evaluation example.

M1.justification: The generic architecture and workflow in Section 5 are retained. Newly discussed systems such as Digi-Q, VEM, and Magma are external methods being reviewed, not additions to an algorithm proposed by this survey.

E1.justification: Neither version conducts model training or evaluation. Added profiles such as SafeArena and WorldGUI expand the benchmark catalogue, without changing datasets or tasks actually used experimentally by the survey.

E2.justification: Neither version evaluates a proposed agent against baselines. The expanded catalogues compare characteristics of published systems, without introducing an experimentally evaluated comparator set.

E3.justification: The evaluation metrics and measurement taxonomy in Sections 9.1–9.2 are retained. Additional benchmark profiles describe other works' settings; the survey introduces no conducted evaluation or revised experimental protocol.

E4.justification: No conducted ablation, robustness analysis, or empirical case study is added. The new AEIA-MN and WorldGUI entries describe evaluation resources, while the new explanatory diagrams illustrate cited approaches.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run uncertainty, seed counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The additional literature summaries introduce no statistical reporting procedure.

E6.justification: v10 adds cited findings: FedMobileAgent achieves comparable performance with cheaper annotation (Section 6.2), PwP can match or surpass tool-based approaches in some scenarios (Section 6.3), and AppVLM is described as providing near-GPT-4o performance while being 10× faster (Table 23). These are newly summarized findings, not same-setting improvements demonstrated by the survey.

T1.justification: Section 5.7.5's MDP formulation is unchanged. The added offline-RL discussion describes cited procedures without adding mathematical definitions, theorems, proofs, or formal derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract, eight research questions in Section 1.2, and conclusion retain the same contribution: a comprehensive survey and practical guide covering GUI-agent foundations, resources, applications, and challenges.

C2.justification: Section 4.4 newly argues that visible GUI actions improve observability and user trust, while API operations can be harder for users to inspect. Added discussion also explains the potential of offline RL to reduce interaction costs. The existing limitations and roadmap remain substantially unchanged.

D1.justification: The expanded catalogues add backbone names, parameter sizes, training-data descriptions, and code pointers for reviewed systems, including Digi-Q/VEM in Table 23 and Magma in Table 26. The survey's own repository and searchable-page access information remains unchanged.

R1.justification: The reviewed literature expands substantially across grounding, federated mobile agents, offline RL, software engineering, and safety or dynamic-environment evaluation. Additions include ECLAIR, FedMobileAgent, PwP, Digi-Q, VEM, Magma, SafeArena, and WorldGUI. Table 2 also adds surveys on automated planning and lifelong learning.

P1.justification: The GUI/API comparison moves from Section 4.3.5 to Section 4.4, and several sections receive explanatory paragraphs and local wording edits. The twelve-section organization and overall narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: v10 adds explanatory Figures 4, 22, and 26. It separates v8's grounding catalogue into model and benchmark Tables 6–7 and expands several framework and model tables into additional parts. Most existing figures and the overall page design are retained.

improvement.justification: The broader technical coverage, clearer GUI/API and RPA illustrations, and separation of grounding models from benchmarks make v10 more useful as a reference. These gains are limited rather than a transformation of the existing synthesis. A small accuracy drawback is the new RWKV-UI row in Table 6, which places '1.6B' under Foundation Model and model names under Size.
